subject: Approximation of a computer model using INLA

messages.author: c10fd4a322aaf349
messages.subject: Approximation of a computer model using INLA
parts:
Hi,

i am trying to use INLA to build a Gaussian Process approximation of a complex spatial computer model. The model takes as inputs a vector of parameter, theta, and some spatial (known) inputs X, and provides as an output a map with some predictions.
I have selected random locations in the map, and now I want to approximate the output of my model using a Gaussian Process where the mean depends linearly on theta and X, taking into account the spatial structure of my outputs.

Here is what my data looks like :
head(d)
          tau        u      upsilon      aW       bW   output   x   y run   x   y   propOSR      propSNH    fc  fc2
0.3054741 4.18219 6.408204   16.71136 1.744384 2.44870 198 171   1 198 171 0.1422347 4.800756e-01  0.19 0.11
0.3054741 4.18219 6.408204   16.71136 1.744384 1.30320 198  21   1 171  21 0.1529917 5.162143e-01  0.19 0.11
0.3054741 4.18219 6.408204   16.71136 1.744384 0.00000 130 112   1 198 112 0.1132591 3.477789e-02 40.00 0.01
0.3054741 4.18219 6.408204   16.71136 1.744384 0.00000  30  81   1 171  81 0.2026594 1.722963e-16  0.01 0.01
0.3054741 4.18219 6.408204   16.71136 1.744384 0.64267 122 109   1 198 109 0.1534018 3.137897e-02  0.02 0.01
0.3054741 4.18219 6.408204   16.71136 1.744384 1.76110  63 159   1 171 159 0.0000000 0.000000e+00  0.19 0.11

for a given run of my computer model, I have the same value for theta (first 5 columns), but I have different locations (x and y) and different values for the spatial inputs (last 4 columns). However, when I run the model with different values for the parameters theta, I am always saving the outputs at the same locations. So in the end, if I run n parameter sets theta_1, ..., theta_n, and save m location points s_1, ..., s_m, I will have n observations at each locations s_1, ..., s_m.

Here is what my code looks like :

locations <- as.matrix(d[,c("x","y")])
mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = locations, max.edge = c(20,50), cutoff = 1)

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh)

A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh = mesh, loc = locations)

mesh.index <- inla.spde.make.index(name="field", n.spde=spde$n.spde)
stack <- inla.stack(data = list(y=d$value),
                    A = list(A,1),
                    effects = list(c(mesh.index,Intercept=1),
                                   list(b0=d$tau, b1=d$u, b2=d$upsilon, b3=d$propOSR, b4=d$propSNH, b5=d$fc)),
                    tag = "est")

formula <- y ~ -1 + Intercept + b0 + b1 + b2 + b3 + b4 + b5 + f(field, model="iid")
res <- inla(formula,
            data = inla.stack.data(stack),
            control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE))


It works fine until I try to project the results on a grid. When I do that using :

gproj = inla.mesh.projector(mesh, xlim=minx:maxx, ylim=miny:maxy)
g.mean = inla.mesh.project(gproj, res$summary.random$field$mean)
g.sd = inla.mesh.project(gproj, res$summary.random$field$sd)

I have the following error message
"Error in projector$proj$A %*% as.vector(field) : Cholmod error 'X and/or Y have wrong dimensions' at file ../MatrixOps/cholmod_sdmult.c, line 90"

I suspect this might arise because I have several observations at the same locations, and so there is a dimension issue. But I havent't been able to solve the problem.

If anyone has an idea or has already done something similar, I would higly appreciate your help!
Thanks
Charlotte

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Approximation of a computer model using INLA
parts:
Where you have f(field, model="iid") you should have f(field, model=spde) instead.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Approximation of a computer model using INLA
parts:
On 12 July 2016 at 15:37, Charlotte Baey <charlot...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thank you for your help. It works now, in the sens that plots are shown.
> However they look very strange ... I am certainly making a mistake
> somewhere. Here is what I have for the posterior mean and standard deviation
> (attached).

>> head(d)
>> tau u upsilon aW bW output x y run
>> x y propOSR propSNH fc fc2
>> 0.3054741 4.18219 6.408204 16.71136 1.744384 2.44870 198 171 1 198 171
>> 0.1422347 4.800756e-01 0.19 0.11

You seem to have two x-columns and two y-columns, which seems a recipe
for confusion with locating the observations. You need to make sure
that you you the same coordinate system for all your location
references.

Here, you should have
xlim=c(minx, maxx)
and similarly for ylim, and again, make sure you're using the same
kinds of coordinates everywhere.
From the pictures you provided, it looks like you somehow zoomed into
a very small region of space

Finn
